stories.title: US debt hits US$40 trillion high, raising ‘doom loop’ risk
stories.summary: Total US public debt surpassed US$40 trillion for the first time, and has now surged by a third in less than five years, as US lawmakers continue to shrug off calls to contend with historically wide financial deficits. stories.title: (3rd LD) Trump says he will meet N. Korea's Kim this year, puts N.K. nukes at 57
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said Wednesday that he will meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-un later this year, while noting that Pyongyang has 57 "very powerful" nuclear weapons, marking the first time he has cited a specific figure for the recalcitrant regime's nuclear arsenal. Trump made the remarks during a press availability at the White House, a day after The Wall Street Journal reported that he is pushing his aides for a meeting with Kim, which could happen during his next trip to Asia, likely to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit set to take place in Shenzhen, China, in November. "Yeah, I will be," Trump told reporters when asked if he is expecting to meet Kim later this year. He did not elaborate on his plan to reengage with Kim. Asked whether he is exchanging written letters with Kim, Trump said, "I can't tell you that." In a separate press availability later, Trump refused to answer a question about whether his goal in reengaging with Kim is still North Korea's denuclearization, raising concerns that his administration could shift its policy focus toward goals short of denuclearization, such as tension reduction and risk management. The Trump administration earlier affirmed its commitment to the "complete" denuclearization of the North. "I don't want to talk about that, but I do have a good relationship with Kim Jong-un as you know, you've seen," Trump said. "He didn't like (Joe) Biden. He didn't like (Barack) Obama. He didn't like anybody, but he likes me." Trump's remarks came amid speculation that he might seek to rekindle his personal diplomacy with Kim, which led to three bilateral meetings during his first term: the first in June 2018 in Singapore, the second in Hanoi in February 2019 and the last at the inter-Korean border village of Panmunjom in June 2019.

stories.title: Unearthing gold bargains in two small Malaysian towns
stories.summary: Kuala Pilah and Port Dickson in Negeri Sembilan offer some of Malaysia’s cheapest gold jewellery, thanks to lower operating costs, simpler designs, and competitive pricing in smaller markets. Gold jewellery can be cheaper in these towns than in Kuala Lumpur, but buyers should consider workmanship charges, purity and buy-back terms to assess the true value. The towns' reputation for affordable gold jewellery spreads through word of mouth and social media, attracting customers from across Malaysia and abroad. KUALA PILAH/PORT DICKSON – When I was preparing to travel to Negeri Sembilan for the recent state election, I expected stories about politics, campaigns and candidates. I did not expect to come home wondering why some of Malaysia’s cheaper places to buy gold jewellery had been hiding in plain sight. It began with a casual tip from a friend who used to live in Negeri Sembilan: that Kuala Pilah was known for selling gold jewellery at prices lower than those in Kuala Lumpur. That piqued my curiosity. There is no single secret behind the town’s reputation. Instead, it appears to come down to the economics of running a jewellery business in a smaller town: lower operating costs, simpler designs and keen competition for a limited pool of customers. There is, however, one misconception worth clearing up. Some Kuala Pilah jewellers say that not being members of the industry’s association gives them greater freedom to set their prices. But Ng Yih Pyng, adviser to the Federation of Goldsmiths and Jewellers Association of Malaysia and group managing director of listed jewellery group Tomei Consolidated, said the association does not set retail prices.
